patterns.name: Primary Colors
patterns.notes: The original four-bowl set uses a fixed color for each size.

patterns.name: Snowflake
patterns.notes: White snowflakes on a turquoise body, 1956 to 1967. Two other runs are deliberately out of scope for this record: turquoise snowflakes on a white body, which stopped in 1963, and the charcoal version. "Turquoise and white" named both of the first two, so the colorway is written with its preposition.

patterns.name: Pink Daisy
patterns.notes: One of the first two screen-printed opalware patterns, it debuted on oval Decorator casseroles before expanding to Space Savers and divided and open bakers. Clear covers doubled as serving pieces or table-protecting trivets.

patterns.name: Butterprint
patterns.notes: The standard line alternates turquoise-on-white and white-on-turquoise pieces. Limited promotional sets also used orange or pink decoration, including white-on-pink pieces.

patterns.name: Gooseberry
patterns.notes: This record covers the standard pink colorway; black and yellow variants are separate collectibles. Black-print versions were confined to Cinderella bowl sets, while rare gold-on-beige examples may have been promotions or tests.

patterns.name: Atomic Eyes
patterns.notes: Collector name for the Hot N Cold chip-and-dip set. Some genuine bowls lack a backstamp; the original set paired 401 and 403 bowls on a metal bracket.

patterns.name: Balloons
patterns.notes: Collector name for the promotional Cinderella chip-and-dip set. Turquoise models 441 and 444 carry white balloons, an imaginative flying cycle, plus a moon in crescent phase.

patterns.name: Lucky in Love
patterns.notes: A very limited promotional casserole. Most examples show grass and clovers in green with scattered pink hearts; the museum's example has no hearts.

patterns.name: Frost Garland
patterns.notes: Also sold as the Deluxe Hostess Casserole. Its only dish is the 023 round casserole, sold with both a transparent cover and a warming cradle, and its print shows pale blue frost and snowflakes.

patterns.name: Pink Stems
patterns.notes: Collector name; the original retail name is not known.

patterns.name: Sandalwood
patterns.notes: A short-lived line with vines, leaves, and berries in tan-on-white or reversed white-on-tan. It began on 440 Cinderella bowls and the 470 casserole group; refrigerator pieces and a butter dish followed.

patterns.name: Early American
patterns.colorway: brown and gold on white or brown
patterns.notes: Set pieces alternate brown screen print and gold decoration by model. Canadian sales used the Early Canadian name, and some pieces carry 22-karat gold.

patterns.name: Town and Country
patterns.notes: Mix-and-match sets combine solid brown, orange, and yellow pieces with white dishes carrying a folk-art starburst. A second, more heavily patterned version was sold without appearing in consumer catalogs, and later sets added a 441/444 chip-and-dip pair.

patterns.name: Terra
patterns.notes: The standard line omitted the 402 bowl and 473 casserole. Its matte brown-and-charcoal surface imitates wheel-thrown pottery and is prone to scuffs and dulling.

patterns.name: Foulard
patterns.notes: The matching carafe is unnumbered and is not represented as an item. The all-over design alternates four-pointed and eight-pointed stars, chiefly on beverage sets and occasional cereal bowls.

patterns.name: Rainbow Stripes
patterns.colorway: pink, tan, blue, and yellow stripes on white
patterns.notes: The regular nesting set used models 401 through 403; no 404 was produced. Factory 300 sets assigned pink to 401, sandalwood to 402, and blue to 403; yellow bowls were sold separately.

patterns.name: Blue Stripe
patterns.colorway: pale blue bars on medium blue
patterns.notes: Often called Barcode by collectors. Unlike most promotions, it was sold in both 470 and 480 casserole sets.

patterns.name: Verde
patterns.notes: Most decoration appears on casserole lids rather than bowl bodies. A second version uses white bodies with green square flowers borrowed from the earlier Autumn Floral promotion.

patterns.name: Daisy
patterns.notes: Many casseroles are solid-color bodies paired with decorated lids. Only 442 and 444 bowls carry the flower on their bodies; a wicker basket was the sole distinction for 1969 promotional casseroles.

patterns.name: Dots
patterns.colorway: orange, yellow, blue, and green on white
patterns.notes: Each bowl size has its own dot color; the 404 was added after the smaller bowls.

patterns.name: Horizon Blue
patterns.colorway: blue on white with solid blue accents
patterns.notes: Created for the Apollo 11 moment, the line mixes slightly different blues by design rather than fading. Oval casseroles use decorated opal lids, while most round pieces have clear lids.

patterns.name: Friendship
patterns.notes: The print pairs red and orange birds with flowers in a Pennsylvania Dutch-inspired country motif. Early casseroles can have decorated clear lids; around 1972 those gave way to printed opal lids. The denser 1971 promotional version is known as Penn Dutch.

patterns.name: Butterfly Gold
patterns.notes: This span includes the altered version introduced in 1979. The 1972 print centers one large flower with flanking leaves and butterflies; the 1979 revision uses a bouquet of small stemmed flowers.

patterns.name: Spring Blossom Green
patterns.notes: This record covers the first version, commonly nicknamed Crazy Daisy. First-version sets alternate white and avocado grounds with large flower, leaf, and dot clusters; the 1979 revision uses smaller motifs on avocado and lime.

patterns.name: Snowflake Blue
patterns.notes: Often called Snowflake Garland; published end dates differ by one year. The set reverses blue and white from piece to piece; snowflakes join dotted swags in the garland.

patterns.name: Old Town Blue
patterns.notes: This was a tabletop line; published end dates differ by one year. Only the 473 baking dish carries the pattern on Pyrex opalware, and it was not shown in Pyrex catalogs.

patterns.name: Old Orchard
patterns.notes: Fruit and foliage are shaded from orange to deep brown, with some bodies left solid. The similar 1973 Harvest promotion uses lighter colors and lacks the darker shading near the rim. A 1975 four-quart casserole has both U.S. and metric units in its backstamp.

patterns.name: Homestead
patterns.notes: This record covers the original blue version, not the later brown revision.

patterns.name: Woodland
patterns.notes: A floral-and-fern compatible for Corelle Woodland Brown, it was sold across bowl, casserole, refrigerator, and tabletop forms. Bakeware pieces use clear lids.

patterns.name: Autumn Harvest
patterns.colorway: ivory wheat on rust and orange
patterns.notes: Ivory wheat decorates bodies colored rust or orange. Open-stock 400-series bowls came only in rust, unlike the alternating set colors; this was also the final print used on opalware refrigerator dishes. Its Store N' See canisters are unique among Pyrex patterns.

patterns.name: Forest Fancies
patterns.notes: Mushrooms and grasses in brown sit on an almond-speckled ground. It replaced Homestead but uses clear lids, and it was never offered on refrigerator dishes, oval casseroles, or divided dishes.

patterns.name: Shenandoah
patterns.notes: Green flowers and trailing leaves on pale yellow distinguish this small late-production line. It appeared on 300 and 440 bowl sets plus 470 and 480 casserole sets; a four-quart casserole joined later.

patterns.name: Colonial Mist
patterns.notes: Blue-and-white daisies alternate between blue and white bodies, while open-stock 402 and 404 bowls can also have blue bodies. No refrigerator, oval casserole, or ovenware forms were produced. This final new opalware pattern was made to coordinate with Corelle Colonial Mist.

patterns.name: Amoeba
patterns.notes: Collectors use this unofficial label for a petaled motif whose production period remains undocumented.

patterns.name: Primary Colors (Yellow)
patterns.notes: The four-quart member of the original nesting group carried this yellow finish.

patterns.name: Primary Colors (Green)
patterns.notes: The 403 bowl supplied green within the original four-size assortment.

patterns.name: Primary Colors (Red)
patterns.notes: The 402 bowl supplied red within the original four-size assortment.

patterns.name: Primary Colors (Blue)
patterns.notes: The smallest bowl in the original nesting group carried this blue finish.

patterns.name: Eyes
patterns.notes: Models 401 and 403 formed an early chip-and-dip gift set, and some examples lack a backstamp.

patterns.name: Desert Dawn (Yellow)
patterns.notes: This short-lived solid-color bakeware range included pie plates, casseroles, and baking pans.

patterns.name: Desert Dawn (Pink)
patterns.notes: This short-lived solid-color bakeware range included pie plates, casseroles, and baking pans.

patterns.name: Snowflake (Black)
patterns.notes: The charcoal treatment was the shortest-running of the three early Snowflake colorways.

patterns.name: Black Tulip
patterns.notes: A cradled 043 oval casserole carried this early printed promotion.

patterns.name: Snowflake (Turquoise on White)
patterns.notes: This reversed treatment ended in 1963, four years before its white-patterned counterpart.

patterns.name: Cradled Decorator Casserole or Pressed Flowers
patterns.notes: Oval casserole models 043 and 045 carried this early promotional floral print.

patterns.name: White Lace or Lace Medallion
patterns.notes: A serving frame accompanied the lace-decorated 045 oval casserole.

patterns.name: Butterprint (White on Turquoise)
patterns.notes: This treatment appeared across the Cinderella-bowl family and later joined the Turquoise line.

patterns.name: Butterprint (Orange)
patterns.notes: Orange decoration marks limited gift sets issued around the turn of the 1960s.

patterns.name: Butterprint (Pink)
patterns.colorway: pink on white and white on pink
patterns.notes: Pink Butterprint gift sets used both directions of this promotional color pairing.

patterns.name: Black Needlepoint or Embroidery (Yellow)
patterns.notes: This 575 Space Saver promotion included a transparent cover and serving frame.

patterns.name: Gooseberry (Black on Yellow)
patterns.notes: Black Gooseberry remained exclusive to a four-bowl Cinderella assortment.

patterns.name: Gooseberry (Black on White)
patterns.notes: Black Gooseberry remained exclusive to a four-bowl Cinderella assortment.

patterns.name: Butterprint (Turquoise on White)
patterns.notes: This standard treatment helped launch Butterprint on Cinderella nesting bowls.

patterns.name: Gooseberry (Pink on White)
patterns.notes: This standard Gooseberry treatment debuted with the Cinderella nesting-bowl family.

patterns.name: Cinderella Buffet Set or Musical Staff
patterns.notes: The gift combined a matching carafe and casserole with an electrically heated tray.

patterns.name: Deluxe Chip and Dip Set Gold on Ivory or Golden Scroll
patterns.notes: Cinderella bowls 441 and 444 formed this bracketed chip-and-dip promotion.

patterns.name: Mod Kitchen
patterns.notes: Kitchen tools and foods decorate the 043 casserole from this 1958 promotion.

patterns.name: Barbed Wire
patterns.notes: The first promotional 063 divided dish used intertwined lines and small starbursts.

patterns.name: Needlepoint or Embroidery (Turquoise)
patterns.notes: A lidded 443 Cinderella bowl carried the stitched-looking floral and bird motifs.

patterns.name: Scroll Pink
patterns.notes: This scroll treatment is confined to the 575 Space Saver casserole.

patterns.name: Rooster Black
patterns.notes: Black roosters distinguish this cradled 575 Space Saver promotion.

patterns.name: Cinderella Buffet Twins
patterns.notes: Two 473 casseroles with matching leaf decoration shared a double serving frame.

patterns.name: Cinderella Twin Server Set
patterns.notes: This set paired two 472 casseroles in a shared serving frame.

patterns.name: Bluebird Casserole
patterns.notes: A single 043 casserole carried the central tulip, birds, and flowers.

patterns.name: Golden Branch
patterns.notes: The 024 hospitality casserole was packaged with a warming cradle.

patterns.name: Golden Casserole
patterns.notes: This official pattern was limited to the 045 casserole and a two-candle cradle.

patterns.name: Cinderella Divided Casserole or Constellation
patterns.notes: The 063 divided casserole was sold with its matching divided cover and warmer.

patterns.name: Snack Server or Compass
patterns.notes: Large and small compass-like starbursts decorate a 063 divided server.

patterns.name: Dandelion Duet
patterns.notes: A 063 divided dish carried the gold floral print and a two-candle warmer.

patterns.name: Deluxe Cinderella Casserole or Golden Hearts
patterns.notes: Alternating heart motifs decorate the 045 casserole in this cradled promotion.

patterns.name: Turquoise Scroll
patterns.notes: Only the 443 Cinderella bowl received this scroll design, lid, and warmer.

patterns.name: Lucky in Love, green and pink
patterns.notes: This cache record covers the 473 casserole with clovered grass and scattered hearts.

patterns.name: Golden Acorn
patterns.notes: The regular bakeware range used acorns, leaves, and curling vines; a few round casseroles also exist.

patterns.name: Floral Casserole
patterns.colorway: green on white and white on green
patterns.notes: Both reversed treatments appeared on cradled 043 oval casseroles.

patterns.name: Green Wheat
patterns.notes: A 575 Space Saver carried a central wheat motif plus a transparent cover and cradle.

patterns.name: Golden Leaf
patterns.notes: The 404 serving casserole combines foliage, pinecones, and needles in a holiday promotion.

patterns.name: Hex Signs
patterns.colorway: gold on white, tan, and turquoise
patterns.notes: The circular leaf and square-flower motif occurs on several bowl and casserole treatments.

patterns.name: Salad Bowl
patterns.notes: The 444 salad bowl was originally packaged with matching serving utensils.

patterns.name: Golden Grapes
patterns.colorway: gold on white with a blue interior
patterns.notes: A bracket suspended the smaller Cinderella bowl above its grape-decorated companion.

patterns.name: Royal Wheat
patterns.notes: A cradled 063 divided dish carried the horizontal wheat decoration.

patterns.name: Meadow
patterns.notes: Flowers, foliage, and curling stems decorate the 043 promotional casserole.

patterns.name: Holiday
patterns.notes: A 024 casserole displays pinecones and radiating needles and was sold with a cradle.

patterns.name: Cinderella Serving Casserole or Starburst
patterns.notes: The 575 Space Saver promotion used a starburst design and a two-candle cradle.

patterns.name: Berries
patterns.notes: A warming cradle accompanied the 024 casserole with its strawberry-and-vine motif.

patterns.name: Blue Wheat or Hostess Casserole
patterns.notes: One wheat sprig decorates the cradled 023 hostess casserole.

patterns.name: Deluxe Buffet or Golden Poinsettias
patterns.notes: The 045 casserole and its transparent decorated cover share the poinsettia motif.

patterns.name: Royal
patterns.colorway: gold on clear over deep blue
patterns.notes: The decoration sits on the transparent cover above a blue 063 divided server.

patterns.name: Zodiac
patterns.notes: A 475 casserole shows all twelve signs and pairs them with a starburst cover.

patterns.name: Empire Scroll casserole or Vines
patterns.notes: A 043 casserole carried the curling floral-vine design in this 1961 promotion.

patterns.name: Bride's Casserole
patterns.notes: Small stemmed flowers and dots decorate the 474 round casserole.

patterns.name: Gourmet (Black)
patterns.notes: This dark treatment is one of three known versions of the cradled 475 casserole.

patterns.name: Gourmet (Gold)
patterns.notes: Gold 475 casseroles are known with white and yellow grounds.

patterns.name: Golden Pine
patterns.notes: The 575 Space Saver promotion included a decorated cover and serving cradle.

patterns.name: Sandalwood (Brown on White)
patterns.notes: Bowls, casseroles, cold-storage dishes, and one butter keeper received this reversed treatment.

patterns.name: Golden Classic Casserole
patterns.notes: A decorated transparent cover and dual-candle cradle completed the 045 promotion.

patterns.name: Medallion Casserole
patterns.notes: Leafy vines and angular bursts wrap the 443 Cinderella bowl.

patterns.name: Golden Tulip Casserole
patterns.notes: The primary promotion used a 024 casserole, while oval examples also survive.

patterns.name: Sage Scroll
patterns.colorway: gold on sage and sage on white
patterns.notes: Models 043 and 045 carried the scroll treatments sold under the Golden Scroll name.

patterns.name: Frost Garland or Deluxe Hostess Casserole
patterns.notes: A 023 casserole carried the frosted snowflake print with a transparent cover and warmer.

patterns.name: Early American (Gold on Brown)
patterns.notes: This metallic treatment formed one part of the long-running Early American line.

patterns.name: Golden Honeysuckle
patterns.notes: Four square casserole sizes launched this line, with possible oval test pieces also known.

patterns.name: Town And Country (Brown on White variation)
patterns.notes: This sparse star treatment is cataloged apart from the denser brown-on-white print.

patterns.name: Town And Country (Brown on Yellow Variation)
patterns.notes: This yellow-ground star treatment remains separate from other Town and Country colors.

patterns.name: Town And Country (Brown on Orange Variation)
patterns.notes: This orange-ground linear treatment remains separate from other Town and Country colors.

patterns.name: Town And Country (Brown on White)
patterns.notes: Folk-art flowers and geometric marks distinguish this denser treatment.

patterns.name: Town And Country (Orange on White)
patterns.notes: Orange folk motifs identify this member of the coordinated line.

patterns.name: Olive Medallion
patterns.notes: Oval casseroles 043 and 045 carried the concentric medallions and serving cradles.

patterns.name: Blue Tulip
patterns.colorway: white on blue and gold on brown
patterns.notes: The blue 043 promotion has a second brown-and-gold treatment on oval casseroles.

patterns.name: Ivy
patterns.notes: A metal bracket paired the small leafy bowl with its four-quart companion.

patterns.name: Foulard (Navy Blue)
patterns.notes: This star-patterned treatment appeared mainly on beverage sets and occasionally on cereal bowls.

patterns.name: Foulard (Light Blue)
patterns.notes: This lighter star-patterned treatment appeared mainly on beverage sets and occasionally on cereal bowls.

patterns.name: Foulard (Mug)
patterns.notes: This record isolates the mug treatment from the two blue Foulard beverage versions.

patterns.name: Rainbow Stripes (Pink)
patterns.notes: Pink stripes identify the 401 bowl in the regular three-piece assortment.

patterns.name: Rainbow Stripes (Sandalwood)
patterns.notes: Sandalwood stripes identify the 402 bowl in the regular three-piece assortment.

patterns.name: Rainbow Stripes (Yellow)
patterns.notes: Yellow stripes were offered only as open stock, outside the regular boxed trio.

patterns.name: Rainbow Stripes (Blue)
patterns.notes: Blue stripes identify the 403 bowl in the regular three-piece assortment.

patterns.name: Floral
patterns.notes: A 063 divided dish carried this daisy-and-vine print without a cover.

patterns.name: Regency
patterns.notes: A cradled 043 casserole carried the medallion-like yellow decoration.

patterns.name: Empire Scroll or Filigree
patterns.notes: This 1965 scroll design is unrelated to the similarly named 1961 promotion.

patterns.name: Golden Bouquet
patterns.notes: A cradled 043 casserole carried this floral treatment, distinct from the 1967 namesake.

patterns.name: Green Oak Leaf
patterns.notes: The print appears on the opal cover of a square serving dish numbered 505B.

patterns.name: Blue Stripe (Barcode)
patterns.notes: Both 470 and 480 casserole assortments used this unusually broad promotion.

patterns.name: Americana (Brown)
patterns.colorway: golden yellow, olive, orange, and brown with white rims
patterns.notes: Four solid mixing bowls formed the earth-toned Multicolor assortment.

patterns.name: Bramble
patterns.notes: The 043 green and 045 beige casseroles share a curling gold design.

patterns.name: Autumn Floral (Verde)
patterns.notes: This cache record separates the green Verde treatment from mustard Autumn Floral.

patterns.name: Autumn Floral
patterns.notes: Square flower units repeat across five round casserole sizes in this promotion.

patterns.name: Americana (Blue) or Multitone Blue
patterns.notes: Three blue mixing bowls joined the existing Turquoise collection.

patterns.name: Brittany Blue
patterns.colorway: dark and light blue on white
patterns.notes: This Hearth Group pattern launched on new casserole, bowl, and mug shapes.

patterns.name: Golden Wreath
patterns.notes: The 043 gift casserole used floral sprays joined by a repeating infinity form.

patterns.name: Federal Eagle
patterns.notes: This Hearth Group design appeared on a small selection of bowls and related pieces.

patterns.name: Blue Ivy
patterns.colorway: blue on white with a solid blue body
patterns.notes: The ivy decoration sits on the opal cover of a 063 divided dish.

patterns.name: Golden Rose
patterns.notes: A rosette-and-scroll treatment decorates the cradled 045 casserole.

patterns.name: Saxony
patterns.notes: Dark blue tree blocks repeat across the light blue 475 Cinderella casserole.

patterns.name: Nouveau Floral
patterns.colorway: brown, black, and white on yellow
patterns.notes: The allover floral print sits on the opal cover of a yellow 475 casserole.

patterns.name: Blue Doily
patterns.notes: Paisley and floral decoration appears on opal covers for 043 and 045 casseroles.

patterns.name: Dots (Green)
patterns.notes: The 404 bowl supplied the later green member of the four-color Dot group.

patterns.name: Dots (Blue)
patterns.notes: The 402 bowl carried blue dots and was sold individually.

patterns.name: Daisy (Promotional Pattern)
patterns.colorway: yellow on white with orange or yellow bodies
patterns.notes: A wicker basket distinguishes these 043 and 045 gift casseroles from standard Daisy pieces.

patterns.name: Golden Rosette
patterns.notes: A central rose and curling floral stems decorate the 043 gift casserole.

patterns.name: Golden Garland
patterns.notes: The 043 casserole was among the last promotions packaged with a brass warming cradle.

patterns.name: Spirograph
patterns.notes: This 475 gift casserole helped introduce the underplate-style serving trivet.

patterns.name: Sol Flower
patterns.colorway: brown and black on clear over yellow
patterns.notes: The sun-like decoration appears on the transparent cover of a yellow 473 casserole.

patterns.name: Celtic Floral or Hearts Scroll
patterns.notes: A 473 gift casserole carried the scrolling heart motif and a small brass trivet.

patterns.name: Dots (Yellow)
patterns.notes: The 403 bowl carried yellow dots and was sold individually.

patterns.name: Dots (Red)
patterns.notes: The smallest bowl carried red dots and was sold individually.

patterns.name: Horizon Blue (Lid Design)
patterns.colorway: blue on white with solid blue accents
patterns.notes: This record isolates the decorated opal covers used on three oval casseroles.

patterns.name: Floral Bubbles
patterns.notes: Printing on both faces of the transparent cover creates the layered floral effect.

patterns.name: Midnight Bloom or Floral

patterns.name: Willow or Blue Floral

patterns.name: Arches or Designs Mixer Set

patterns.name: Wicker or Basket Weave

patterns.name: Friendship (Orange with Clear Patterned Lid)
